title: Manufacturing and Trade: Inventories and Sales (August 2026 data) — the first combined business-inventories print on the restated retail basis, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 1,135 table rows parsed across the 2020-2026 pages), row "Manufacturing and Trade: Inventories and Sales | October 15, 2026 | 10:00 AM | August 2026", release code A202610151000, reference A202608 — the 82nd MTIS release on the archive this session rebuilt. Corroborated word-for-word on census.gov/mtis/index.html the same day: "Revisions to the retail estimates are anticipated to be reflected in the August 2026 MTIS release scheduled for October 15, 2026." Further corroborated by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet, whose 2026-10-15 row reads "Retail sales + inventories, Producer Price Index". Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, and because Census's own restatement wording is "anticipated". Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, after reading the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/mtis-2026-10-15.from-mwts-benchmark-revision-2026-10-26.json, now shadowed and inert). Every claim in that proposal was re-derived this session and all survive. The identity: this is the edition Census names as the one where the 2023/2024 AIES RETAIL restatement reaches the combined business-inventories series — retail is 30.4% of inventories and 31.5% of sales at June-2026 weights, so from 2026-10-15 that share stands on the new basis while wholesale waits for 2026-11-17 and manufacturers stays frozen by the M3 special notice for the remainder of 2026. One correction this session establishes on two program-page primaries: census.gov/retail dates BOTH the revised not-adjusted AND the corresponding adjusted retail estimates to 2026-09-28, and census.gov/wholesale dates both wholesale bases to 2026-10-26 — so the compressed "September 28, 2026 and October 26, 2026, respectively" on census.gov/mtis binds to the two SURVEYS, not to the two adjustment bases. This print therefore has no unpublished dependency: its retail input publishes in full seventeen days ahead of it. Same-date collision caution as every MTIS entry: a tracked entry already occupies 2026-10-15 and it is a different release — retail-sales-2026-10-15 is the 08:30 Advance Monthly Retail Trade report for SEPTEMBER data (A202610150830, reference A202609), while this is the 10:00 MTIS for AUGUST data (A202610151000, reference A202608). MTIS has never once printed without that 08:30 companion (84 of 84). Impact LOW and symbols empty on measured grounds: no house playbook is macro-keyed (grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-run 2026-09-06, 0 hits) and no instrument attaches. Date stays estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
